answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Dodoco Blast first, spending 2 Sparks to deal 7 damage to all enemies, killing Twig Slime (S) and reducing both Leaf Slimes. Then I played Kaboom! on Leaf Slime (S), killing it. Finally I played Duck and Cover for 5 Block. I left 1 Energy unused.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I considered playing Bang Bang! instead of Dodoco Blast, since it also costs 0 and spends 2 Sparks, but its 5 damage twice to random enemies is less controlled and lower total than Dodoco Blast's 7 damage to all enemies, so I rejected it.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up the 2 Spark bank for future turns and the chance to use Bang Bang!'s random hits. It also left 1 Energy unused, and the 5 Block may be wasted if the remaining Leaf Slime (M) does not attack.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. If the Leaf Slime (S) were not an immediate attacker or the Leaf Slime (M) telegraphed a larger attack, I would likely retarget Kaboom! at the higher-priority enemy; Dodoco Blast and Duck and Cover would probably remain.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
